status.detail: Two reports were supplied; the extracted stack is a WPF render-thread failure on the secondary monitor.

next_action.label: Compare GPU rendering paths
next_action.reason: The author already answered the driver-update question; isolate the rendering backend rather than asking again.

judgment.rationale: The secondary-monitor layout editing sequence, hybrid-GPU topology and concrete UCEERR_RENDERTHREADFAILURE stack support a maintainer-side rendering comparison. The author supplied the follow-up report and explained that drivers were already current.
evidence: The primary monitor uses Radeon RX 570; the secondary uses Intel i5-8400 integrated graphics.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/16499#issuecomment-1055663423 supplies the requested newer report after 0.56.1 also exits.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/16499#issuecomment-1065321885 explains the installed drivers and rejects unnecessary driver changes.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with two GPU-driven monitors and compare hardware/software rendering in an isolated diagnostic build.

fix_assessment.rationale: The render-thread stack justifies investigating editor rendering resilience. It does not prove a GPU-driver defect or justify declaring external ownership.

proposed_fixes.title: Isolate and mitigate FancyZones Editor composition failure
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: WPF hardware composition fails when the editor renders added zones on the Intel-driven secondary monitor in a mixed-GPU system. The WPF render-thread failure is confirmed; the specific hardware/driver interaction is not.
plan: Reproduce adding/resizing zones on each monitor with the reported topology, collecting the exception signature from both supplied reports and a current build.
Use an isolated diagnostic build of src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesEditor to compare normal WPF rendering with software rendering; do not change the machine's global rendering settings.

If the backend comparison confirms the hypothesis, design a narrowly scoped supported fallback or recovery path and preserve the unsaved layout during failure; do not attempt to resume a fatally failed WPF render thread by swallowing the exception.
Add coverage for layout-state preservation and verify any fallback on both GPUs before deciding whether runtime/driver escalation is needed.
verification: Create, add, resize, save and reopen layouts independently on both monitors without crashing or losing zones.
Compare hardware and diagnostic software rendering; record if the exception persists so an ineffective fallback is not shipped.

confidence.rationale: The stack locates a rendering failure, but there is no controlled backend comparison and a fallback may not address the underlying cause.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones Editor crashes or exits while adding zones on the secondary, integrated-GPU monitor, losing unsaved changes.
known_information: Reported on 0.55.2 and again on 0.56.1, Windows 10 21H1.
The author supplied both requested diagnostic archives.
The extracted stack identifies WPF composition failure.
The author says drivers are already current; the issue is open and unassigned.
inferences: Hybrid-GPU composition is a useful discriminator, not a confirmed external hardware fault.
issue_context.analysis: There is sufficient public environment detail for a targeted maintainer experiment. Repeating the generic ZIP or driver request would ignore the responses.
initial_investigation: Read the report and all eight comments, including the newer report and driver response.
No linked concrete fix appears in the issue timeline.
The supplied stack originates in WPF composition rather than a demonstrated zone-count validation exception.

reproduce.title: Secondary-monitor zone editing render failure
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare historical 0.55.2/0.56.1 evidence with a current supported build.
prerequisites: Two physical monitors, one on Intel integrated graphics and one on a discrete GPU
Record GPU drivers and display arrangement; preserve existing layouts.
steps: 1. Create a new layout for the secondary Intel-driven monitor.
2. Add several zones, then resize and reposition them and save.
3. Repeat on the primary monitor and compare the exception signature to the supplied WPF stack.
4. In an isolated diagnostic build, repeat with WPF software rendering and compare stability and save persistence.
reproduce.expected_result: Editing and saving succeeds on both monitors; the comparison establishes whether backend selection changes the failure.

actions.label: Review provisional editor rendering plan
actions.note: Prove the backend distinction before selecting a mitigation.
